jobs.title: 照料母亲
jobs.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. One edge-to-edge landscape 16:9 live-action narrative movie frame, no collage, no borders. It must look photographed in an inhabited poor Caribbean port town in the late 1760s or early 1770s: humidity, rough limewash, ordinary worn timber, cloth actually used, uneven available light, natural color and medium depth of field. People are occupied with concrete tasks, with ordinary awkward body positions; camera has found somewhere to stand. No painterly render, no oil-painting composition, no theatrical lighting, no heroic portrait, no staged still life, no golden dust, no sepia, no teal-orange grade, no beauty retouching, no modern objects, no readable text, no captions or watermark. The reference is ONLY for the named identity or environment role; it is never a request to reproduce a collage or portrait-board format. Reference role: face identity ONLY of the boy, same slender child of about eleven in visual casting, olive complexion, brown eyes and loose neck-length dark brown hair. Do not copy reference studio light, clean outfit finish or pose.
A low cramped Caribbean dwelling, daylight. Camera stands just inside a doorway at adult chest height, about 3m from a low simple wooden bed along the right wall; 35mm ordinary perspective. Partial near doorpost on extreme left, scratched stool at bedside, worn but usable plaster and wood shutter, thin well-used cream bedding, a little dirty green banana foliage glimpsed through a small open window, no elaborate furniture. A rough table corner is cropped in the lower left. Keep this layout simple and specific so it can recur.
The mother is a living adult woman in her thirties, worn ordinary off-white linen shift, dark hair carelessly tied back. She is tired and mildly unwell but awake, sitting propped by folded bedding. Her face is mostly in side view, no glamour, no dramatic symptoms, no wounds. The boy is standing partly back to camera at the bedside, in a faded brown vest, worn linen shirt and brown knee breeches; he is carefully lowering a small plain brown ceramic water bowl toward the scratched bedside stool, bowl still held in BOTH his hands just above the stool. Mother's near hand rests quietly on the blanket, not reaching for the bowl. A small gray washing cloth rests over the edge of the bowl. Their attention is on the ordinary task, no staged eye contact or overt sadness.
Expose for the dim room, daylight window somewhat brighter without a halo. Sweat-darkened collars, minor uneven repairs, wall wear concentrated near window and floor, some intact useful things. A real unpolished domestic care moment, not a historical painting, not a sickroom theatre tableau. Do not show a body under a shroud or any funeral scene.

It must look photographed in an inhabited poor Caribbean port town in the late 1760s or early 1770s: humidity, rough limewash, ordinary worn timber, cloth actually used, uneven available light, natural color and medium depth of field. No painterly render, no oil-painting composition, no theatrical lighting, no heroic portrait, no staged still life, no golden dust, no sepia, no teal-orange grade, no beauty retouching, no modern objects, no readable text, no captions or watermark. The reference is ONLY for the named identity or environment role; it is never a request to reproduce a collage or portrait-board format. Reference role: same teen's face, civilian clothing and the same modest tropical dwelling's materials, BEFORE the roof damage shown in reference. Generate a new camera angle during a storm, not the beam-lifting scene. Keep exact youthful long face, brown eyes, dark brown wavy hair tied low, clean-shaven, sweat-damp unbleached shirt, open charcoal-brown waistcoat and worn brown breeches. No pristine portrait grooming.
During a violent late-afternoon tropical rainstorm, camera is inside the cramped room at chest height, 35mm lens, looking at an old two-leaf vertical-board wooden shutter. The shutter is on the left half of the frame, latched but bowing inward a very small amount. Teen right of center in partial SIDE-BACK view, already bracing it with his left shoulder and both palms, knees flexed, one foot half a step behind the other for real leverage. He watches the wood and his hands, face partly turned away and naturally shadowed. Both feet have clear floor contact. Shutter construction and hand contact must be simple and mechanically plausible.
A narrow streak of rain comes through the gap; no flying wreckage, no collapsing walls, no burst glass, no floating papers. A corner of a working wooden table with closed books is visible bottom right, safely clear of the shutter swing; roof still intact. The wall around the window is damp, but objects not all uniformly ruined.
Actual overcast storm daylight through narrow gaps, dim but readable skin and wood, natural wet green hint outside, low contrast exterior without lightning theatrics. Frame is a practical view of someone holding pressure against weather, not an elegant sideways portrait. Same Caribbean material world as reference, tighter untidy crop, no full beautifully arranged room.

jobs.title: 文章获得支持
jobs.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. One edge-to-edge landscape 16:9 live-action narrative movie frame, no collage, no borders. It must look photographed in an inhabited poor Caribbean port town in the late 1760s or early 1770s: humidity, rough limewash, ordinary worn timber, cloth actually used, uneven available light, natural color and medium depth of field. People are occupied with concrete tasks, with ordinary awkward body positions; camera has found somewhere to stand. No painterly render, no oil-painting composition, no theatrical lighting, no heroic portrait, no staged still life, no golden dust, no sepia, no teal-orange grade, no beauty retouching, no modern objects, no readable text, no captions or watermark. The reference is ONLY for the named identity or environment role; it is never a request to reproduce a collage or portrait-board format. Reference role: visual texture, worn functional Caribbean commercial interior and natural exposure ONLY. The adolescent in reference is NOT in this frame. A different dry desk corner in an ordinary countinghouse, several days after the rain, with an open doorway beyond the left showing a sunlit cargo yard and indistinct working activity.
Camera from close to a desk corner at chest height, ordinary 40mm perspective. One unglamorous male adult reader of roughly fifty sits on the far right side of the desk, in a faded civilian linen shirt and plain worn brown waistcoat, no powdered wig. He is already reading ONE gray-white sheet held tilted away from camera in his LEFT hand; the back of the sheet faces camera, no readable writing. His RIGHT hand holds a small dark leather money pouch a few centimeters above the table, clearly suspended, not resting on the table. His gaze stays on the sheet, no smiling, nodding or portrait pose. Hands must be separated and anatomically credible.
Beside him on the near-left part of the table sits a travel bundle: patched gray-brown unbleached linen bag with a simple cloth shoulder strap, flat roughly oval patch near its lower outside corner. The bag is ordinary and partly filled, shoulder strap lying casually on the desk. The pouch, paper and travel bag must all be visible in the same space. One plain folded coat alongside the bag, not a decorative still life. No youth waiting to be paid, no hand-to-hand money transaction, no merchant scales.
A cropped sack or box at the extreme left foreground, desks with localized finger and edge wear, roughly limewashed wall and patched shutters, ordinary dry daylight. No evenly aged antique parchment: the sheet is relatively fresh gray-white rag paper, not ancient brown relic material. Quiet actual reading and a practical means for travel, with the camera incidentally nearby. The travel bag is a continuity prop to repeat in a later boarding scene.
